_account: FTMO Demo, USD 50,000, DEMO. Symbol is XAUUSD (no 'm' suffix) with 2 digits; resolve_symbol handles the name and value_per_point works out to 100.0.
_measured_week: Measured from 4,000 FTMO M15 bars, not assumed: the last bar of the week opens Fri 23:45 and closes Sat 00:00 server, and the first opens Mon 01:00. Seven of nine weeks agreed; the two that ended Fri 20:00 were short weeks. There are no Saturday bars at all. So gold's 21:00 UTC close lands at 00:00 Saturday on this UTC+3 server -- which is why the close weekday is 5 and the hour is 0, not Friday 23:00. Re-measure in winter, when FTMO moves to UTC+2 (EET) and the close becomes Fri 23:00.
_comment_offset: Measured UTC+3 from a live tick (EEST). Only used while the market is shut and the offset cannot be measured. Becomes 2.0 in winter; the bot re-measures on its own whenever quotes are flowing.
_measured_spread: FTMO's median gold spread is $0.40 on M15 and $0.42 on M30, against $0.20 in the Exness data the backtest was built on -- double. It costs less than it sounds: gold's R is $11-16, so the extra is +0.012 to +0.018R per trade and M15's holdout expectancy goes from +0.156R to about +0.140R. This is why gold survived the cost correction and the FX pairs did not: their R was small enough that spread ate the edge outright.
_comment_risk: 0.40% is the smallest risk that still splits three ways on a 10,000 balance: at 0.25% the size rounds down to a single 0.02 leg, and one leg exiting at TP2 is not the exit the lab measured. Below this the system being run stops being the system that was tested.
_comment_risk_ruin: Measured by sweeping expectancy through the simulator rather than trusting M15's own train split, which sits entirely inside the 2024-25 gold bull market and is therefore no stress test. At +0.156R/trade -- the recent regime -- Step 1 passes 100% of paths. At +0.003R/trade, what gold M30 actually printed through the flat 2023, Step 1 passes 32% and 28% of paths hit the 10% max loss first. Ruin risk here is set by whether the edge holds, not by the risk percentage.
_comment_risk_size: A 25,000 account at 0.25% does NOT buy safety: in the same flat case it passes 24.9% and ruins 20.3%, slightly worse, because a smaller risk needs more trades to reach +10% and so spends longer inside the random walk. Account size is not the lever; measuring real cost is.
_comment_exit: Capital tier is anchored to the account's initial balance, not live balance/equity: below 30,000 uses one leg to fixed TP3; 30,000 or above requires three executable 33/33/34 legs and, only after TP1 is confirmed closed, moves each survivor to its actual broker fill plus commission, slippage, and cumulative negative swap. The stop is refreshed while survivors remain open; positive swap never loosens it. The active policy never flips while an account is running.
_comment_timeframes: M15 + M30, both on the pinned fixed_tp3 exit above.
_comment_timeframes_why: M30 added 28 Jul 2026 to lift frequency from 1.9 to 2.8 trades/day. It earns the slot on evidence, not frequency: 4.2 years of data covering the flat 2023, and the highest expectancy of any stream tested (+0.299R against M15's +0.156R). A second SYMBOL was rejected instead -- USDJPY and GBPUSD sit at +0.03 to +0.07R and would dilute the book, and running every qualifying stream at once produced a worst day of -5.11%, which breaches the 5% daily loss rule on its own.
_comment_news: Fail closed for production safety: if the high-impact USD calendar is unavailable or stale, existing positions remain managed but no new entry is allowed.
_comment_tags: The concrete exit tag (fixedtp3 or be33) is appended by trader.py after resolving the capital tier.
_comment_closures: Holidays and early closes on the server clock, maintained by hand because MT5 5.0.5735 exposes no session schedule. These spans are deliberately generous and are ESTIMATES -- confirm them against FTMO's own notice before December. Being an hour too wide costs a skipped trade; being an hour too narrow is a forbidden-practice breach. A span shorter than two hours is ignored, since the gap-trading rule does not reach it.
